Architecture ​

FaultDeck is a Rust workspace. The current implementation ships six built crates plus one empty placeholder (faultdeck-protocol — the directory exists but contains no Cargo.toml and is not a workspace member yet). The planned toxiproxy backend and scenario YAML DSL from the MVP plan are not implemented; today's backend is tc netem + iptables.

Crates ​

cratebinaryresponsibility
faultdeck-core—shared model: FaultSpec (latency / loss / disconnect), Target, Injection, intrinsic validation (validate_injection), management-network overlap check
faultdeck-netem—tc adapter: plans and executes tc qdisc/filter commands, preflight checks, rollback, dry_run executor
faultdeck-agentfaultdeck-agentresident TCP daemon: token auth, request handling, iptables firewall (disconnect), single-active-fault state
faultdeck-coordinatorfaultdeck-coordinatormulti-target hub: agent registry (register/heartbeat/list with online status), report archive, live inject/rollback dispatch over agent reverse links, per-agent queues for offline agents
faultdeck-report—Scenario, RunReport (JSON/HTML), SHA-256 scenario hash, compare_runs history diff
faultdeck-clifaultdeckCLI entry: faultdeck remote ping / inject / rollback (direct to agent) and faultdeck hub list / inject / rollback (via coordinator)
faultdeck-protocol—placeholder, not in workspace

Wire protocol (CLI ↔ agent) ​

One TCP connection per CLI invocation. The client sends a single line; the agent answers with a single JSON line and closes.

  • With token: <token> {json}\n — without: {json}\n
  • Request: {"cmd":"ping"} | {"cmd":"inject", ...Injection} | {"cmd":"rollback"}
  • Response: {"status":"ok","message":"..."} | {"status":"error","message":"..."}

Wire protocol (coordinator) ​

Long-lived connections, newline-framed JSON lines in both directions (faultdeck-agent::transport). One listener serves two session kinds, disambiguated by the first frame:

  • Controller session — a WireMessage envelope per command. AgentCommand: register | heartbeat | inject | rollback | fetch_report | list_agents; AgentResponse: ok | error | registered | queued | agents | report.
  • Agent link — the agent dials the coordinator outbound (double-NAT safe) and sends a RegisterEnvelope first (crates/agent/src/link.rs:46); afterwards the coordinator writes LinkMessage::Dispatch frames down the same connection and the agent answers with LinkMessage::Result plus periodic LinkMessage::Heartbeats.

State lives in a Mutex<CoordinatorState>: agents, reports, links (live reverse connections), and per-agent queues are BTreeMaps.

Implementation status: inject/rollback validate, archive a report stub, and then dispatch for real — a live link receives the command immediately, the agent's execution result is returned to the waiting controller (bounded by DEFAULT_DISPATCH_TIMEOUT, 5 s) and folded into the archived report; if the agent is offline the command persists in its queue and is drained on its next registration. list_agents annotates each AgentIdentity.online from link liveness or heartbeat freshness (HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_MS, 30 s) and offline agents are excluded from available.

Failure handling in the netem adapter ​

  1. plan() validates and returns the command list without executing.
  2. inject() runs a preflight tc qdisc show — refuses to touch an interface whose root qdisc is not FaultDeck's 100: handle.
  3. Any leftover FaultDeck root qdisc is cleaned up before applying.
  4. If any command fails mid-apply, the adapter immediately issues the rollback command.
  5. rollback() deletes the root qdisc; "not found"-style tc errors are tolerated (idempotent).

Disconnect faults bypass tc entirely — see Netem Faults.

Source layer map ​

The source responsibility layers are independent of crate-directory names. Terms are synchronized in the Glossary.

1. Shared semantics and safety model ​

crates/core/src/lib.rs owns FaultSpec, Target, Injection, intrinsic validation, and management-network overlap checks (crates/core/src/lib.rs:26, crates/core/src/lib.rs:44, crates/core/src/lib.rs:82, crates/core/src/lib.rs:108, crates/core/src/lib.rs:142). It is persistent-state-free and has no network I/O. Its schema is Rust Serde plus the intrinsic validation errors at crates/core/src/lib.rs:88; fault-facing prose is in Netem Faults, and no dedicated protocol file exists.

2. Policy-to-backend translation ​

crates/netem/src/lib.rs translates validated latency/loss into ordered tc qdisc and filter commands through NetemAdapter (crates/netem/src/lib.rs:172, crates/netem/src/lib.rs:199, crates/netem/src/lib.rs:204). Its execution port is CommandExecutor (crates/netem/src/lib.rs:73), the command schema is TcCommand (crates/netem/src/lib.rs:56), and runtime inputs are the interface name plus the optional dry-run executor setting (crates/netem/src/lib.rs:172, crates/netem/src/lib.rs:80). It stores no state between calls and exposes no network protocol; implementation detail is in Architecture.

3. Host execution and guard ​

crates/agent/src/lib.rs is the agent host: it accepts TCP, authenticates, guards management CIDRs, decodes requests, routes disconnect or netem, and keeps the active-fault marker in Arc<Mutex<HashSet<String>>> (crates/agent/src/lib.rs:171, crates/agent/src/lib.rs:326, crates/agent/src/lib.rs:340). Its config schema is AgentConfig (crates/agent/src/lib.rs:90), populated by crates/agent/src/main.rs:9; Configuration documents those inputs. The Iptables backend in crates/agent/src/firewall.rs:31 executes host rules, while protocol types remain in crates/agent/src/lib.rs:109 and crates/agent/src/lib.rs:117; no dedicated protocol file exists.

4. Wire transport and topology ​

crates/agent/src/transport.rs owns bounded NDJSON framing plus Mode A listen/accept and Mode B reverse connect (crates/agent/src/transport.rs:56, crates/agent/src/transport.rs:94, crates/agent/src/transport.rs:118). It is stateless except accepted sockets. The framing schema is the generic send_frame/read_frame pair (crates/agent/src/transport.rs:57, crates/agent/src/transport.rs:65). On top of that framing, crates/agent/src/link.rs implements the live Mode B link session — register envelope, heartbeat thread, dispatch pump, and the reconnecting run_link loop (crates/agent/src/link.rs:77, crates/agent/src/link.rs:140, crates/agent/src/link.rs:184). Topology prose is in Agents, and payload types live in the agent and coordinator layers rather than a dedicated protocol crate (crates/protocol/src is empty).

5. User boundary and report materialization ​

crates/cli/src/main.rs converts remote ping/inject/rollback and hub list/inject/rollback arguments into shared Injection values, performs bounded TCP exchanges with the agent or coordinator, optionally materializes JSON/HTML reports, and generates a replay command (crates/cli/src/main.rs:136, crates/cli/src/main.rs:165, crates/cli/src/main.rs:227, crates/cli/src/main.rs:341). It owns no server state; file output is caller-directed. The command schema is the clap tree at crates/cli/src/main.rs:22, FAULTDECK_TIMEOUT_SECS is the sole environment input (crates/cli/src/main.rs:236), and user-facing flags are documented in Configuration.

6. Fleet registry and control-plane state ​

crates/coordinator/src/lib.rs runs a threaded TCP hub, stores agents, reports, live links, and per-agent queues in Arc<Mutex<CoordinatorState>>, and handles controller sessions plus agent reverse links (crates/coordinator/src/lib.rs:156, crates/coordinator/src/lib.rs:270, crates/coordinator/src/lib.rs:455, crates/coordinator/src/lib.rs:503). All state is volatile. AgentIdentity, AgentCommand, AgentResponse, and WireMessage define that schema (crates/coordinator/src/lib.rs:51, crates/coordinator/src/lib.rs:69, crates/coordinator/src/lib.rs:80, crates/coordinator/src/lib.rs:235); crates/coordinator/src/main.rs:4 supplies bind/token inputs documented in Configuration. Agents carries the operational protocol prose.

7. Evidence and reproducibility model ​

crates/report/src/lib.rs owns Scenario, scenario hashing, RunReport, HTML rendering, timestamps, and report comparison (crates/report/src/lib.rs:38, crates/report/src/lib.rs:49, crates/report/src/lib.rs:78, crates/report/src/lib.rs:110, crates/report/src/lib.rs:168, crates/report/src/lib.rs:182). It is persistent-state-free; CLI and coordinator decide whether to retain output. Its Serde schema is the report model itself, HTML copy is generated in the same layer, and dedicated user prose is in Reports.

Why these layers are split ​

  1. core::Injection is consumed by both direct CLI construction and coordinator validation, so semantic validation must not depend on either transport host (crates/cli/src/main.rs:136, crates/coordinator/src/lib.rs:309).
  2. Netem exposes plan, inject, and rollback separately; the agent needs execution while adapters and tests need dry planning or recorded commands (crates/netem/src/lib.rs:199, crates/netem/src/lib.rs:204, crates/netem/src/lib.rs:232).
  3. The netem executor is a trait so the same command translation can target Linux tc, dry-run, or a test recorder without changing policy (crates/netem/src/lib.rs:73, crates/netem/src/lib.rs:163).
  4. Disconnect and packet faults differ in state, atomicity, and rollback mechanics; the agent routes them to separate Iptables and NetemAdapter implementations (crates/agent/src/lib.rs:196, crates/agent/src/firewall.rs:117, crates/netem/src/lib.rs:204).
  5. The agent's active-fault marker lives across connections, but the command executor socket handle is accepted per connection; mixing those lifetimes would make recovery state accidental (crates/agent/src/lib.rs:340, crates/agent/src/lib.rs:341).
  6. Coordinator state and dispatch routing are centralized separately from target execution: the hub turns a controller command into a LinkMessage::Dispatch on the agent's reverse channel (or queues it while the agent is offline), while the agent crate owns actual fault application (crates/coordinator/src/lib.rs:351, crates/coordinator/src/lib.rs:660).
  7. Reports require stable hashes, replay text, and evidence fields independent of whether the caller stores them in a file or coordinator memory (crates/report/src/lib.rs:49, crates/report/src/lib.rs:92, crates/cli/src/main.rs:233).
